subject: Measurement & temporary-exception questions for production SLOs
messages:
From: Samira Ghazal <samira@parhelion.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement: SLO measurement + temporary exception questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement asked us to send a short set of questions so they can map Redwood's commitments into our legal/operations review. Attached is our standard SLO questionnaire (Parhelion_SLO_Questionnaire.xlsx). High-level asks:

- How is availability measured (what endpoints, what success criteria)?
- What latency percentiles are guaranteed (p95/p99)? How are they calculated over rolling windows?
- Do you provide customer-facing dashboards or a read-only Grafana link?
- What alerting integrations are supported (PagerDuty, email, webhook)?
- Is there a documented exception path for scheduled maintenance or temporary telemetry gaps?

We're also running a short pilot that requires a temporary exception for inbound telemetry collection (third-party agent limitations on our side). Procurement wants to understand how that exception would be handled operationally and what evidence we can get for the audit.

Can you point us to a concise doc or answer inline? We'd like to close this in the next five business days.

Thanks,
Samira
Procurement Lead, Parhelion Labs
procure@parhelion.io

Attachment: Parhelion_SLO_Questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 4 sheets)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>

Hi Samira — thanks for sending this over and for the clear questions. Quick replies below, and I'm looping in Marissa (your AE) and Logan (infra/ops) for the technical and exception details. We can book a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through the answers.

Quick answers:
- Availability: defined as successful completion of API requests (2xx) to the production inference endpoints for the model variant you pin; we exclude customer-requested maintenance windows and pre-announced capacity maintenance.
- Latency: we publish p95 and p99 over a rolling 30-day window by default; we can offer alternative windows for contract definitions.
- Dashboards: we offer a read-only Grafana view for enterprise customers (invite-based), plus periodic CSV reports for audits.
- Alerting: integrations: PagerDuty, Slack, email, and generic webhook. We can route alerts to an existing Parhelion PagerDuty service with a short verification.
- Exceptions: short-term telemetry gaps (e.g., third-party collector restrictions) are handled via a documented exception flow — typically a temporary monitoring carveout plus enhanced post-window evidence (logs, traces, and token-level latency dumps).

I've attached a brief overview (SLA-Measurement-Overview.pdf). Marissa/Logan — can you add the measurement and exception specifics (retention, sampling, evidence artifacts) and confirm whether we can provide a Grafana invite for Parhelion's pilot?

Next steps:
1) Marissa to confirm commercial attachment (what we can commit contractually).
2) Logan to specify retention/exports and the exception workflow.
3) Book 30-min call if Parhelion wants a walkthrough.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-Measurement-Overview.pdf (3 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO measurement + temporary exception questions

Hi Samira — appreciated, and happy to help close this out for procurement. I'll keep this high level so it can slot into their review doc.

Measurement summary (what we'd include contractually):
- Availability (Uptime) definition: % of successful 2xx requests across production inference endpoints for the selected model family and region, sampled at the edge prior to retries. Measurement window: rolling 30-day and monthly calendar windows reported.
- Latency: we report p50/p95/p99 for token-generation time and request-complete latency. Contractual commitments usually reference p95 over a rolling 30-day baseline with a remediation credit if we miss the monthly threshold.
- Sampling & guards: short spikes from customer-side network issues are excluded by correlating client IP traces and our edge ingress logs. We document known exclusion criteria in the SLO appendix.
- Maintenance & scheduled work: pre-announced maintenance windows (we provide at least 48 hours for non-emergency) are excluded from availability calculations. Emergency maintenance is handled case-by-case; we provide evidence and post-incident write-up.
- Evidence artifacts: time-series metrics (Prometheus), aggregated CSV extracts for the contractual window, raw request logs for audit (redacted as needed), and a short attestation statement signed by our ops lead.

Operational & access notes:
- Grafana invites: yes — read-only, time-limited as requested. We can also grant a longer-term viewer role for the contract term.
- Alerting: direct PagerDuty integration is supported; we need the target PD service key to verify routing. We can also send webhooks to procurement tooling.
- Retention: default metrics retention is 365 days for aggregated metrics and 90 days for raw request logs; longer retention can be contracted as an add-on for audits.

Exception workflow (for your pilot telemetry restriction):
1) Customer files an exception request via the procurement ticket (procure@parhelion.io) with dates and reason.
2) We approve a time-boxed carveout (typical: 14–30 days) and provide a compensating evidence package covering the period (CSV extracts + token-level latency snapshots).
3) During the carveout we enable heightened sampling on neighboring nodes to minimize blind spots.
4) Post-carveout we produce an attestation and discuss any contractual remediation if SLOs are impacted.

I've attached our internal "MA-Request-Checklist.pdf" which procurement teams find useful; it lists evidence formats and SLA clause language we typically accept.

Let me know if you want me to draft a short clause you can insert into the SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MA-Request-Checklist.pdf (2 pages)
Related link: https://hubspot.company/contacts/PHL-2026-43

Hi Samira — Logan from Infra/Observability here. Quick technical clarifications and what we can commit for the pilot/exception: 

Retention & exports:
- We can retain raw request logs for the carveout period for up to 180 days as a contracted add-on (requires a short Data Retention Addendum). Default raw retention is 90 days; aggregated metrics are 365 days.
- Weekly CSV exports: yes — we can push CSVs to a secure SFTP or to your shared Drive folder. Format: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, region, status_code, request_latency_ms, token_count.

Grafana scoping:
- Invite scope: we can create a panel-only role limited to the production inference dashboards (no billing or internal admin panels). Access is strictly read-only and can be time-bounded in the invite. We will provide a "redwood-grafana-invite-stub.txt" (invite instructions) once procurement confirms the user list.

Alerting and PagerDuty:
- We support PD, Slack, email, and webhook. For PD we will require the integration service key during onboarding and will do a short verification run (test alert).

Sampling / measurement notes:
- p95/p99 calculation: we compute percentiles on completed request latencies after edge retries within the chosen window; transient network failures from your side are correlated and excluded when clearly attributable.
- Test sample: we can run a 7-day performance smoke with a reserved small-capacity burst (up to X rps) and provide the p99 sample. There is a one-time resourcing fee if the reservation exceeds current pilot quotas; we'll itemize if you request it.

Exception handling process (summary):
1) Procurement opens exception ticket with dates and scope.
2) Infra approves carveout with required compensating controls.
3) We enable enhanced sampling and produce weekly CSV exports during the window.
4) Post-window: infra provides an attestation + exported evidence package for audit ingestion.

If you want, I can stand up the Grafana invite and a sample CSV export within 48 hours of procurement approval — send me the list of viewer emails and the SFTP/Drive target.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-grafana-invite-stub.txt (instructions).
